notes: Each story has metadata + a position (% of room width/height) for its hotspot in the painted scene. Story text lives at stories/<id>.md and is lazy-loaded on click. Every trinket is a book — each hotspot points to a specific painted book in the room (bookshelf, windowsill, or floor stack). Plants/photos/etc. are reserved for future stories.

stories.contentNote: A Squamish legend, told to Pauline Johnson by Chief Joe Capilano, 1911. The Squamish name for The Lions is Ch'ích'iyúy Elx̱wíḵn — Twin Sisters.
stories.summary: The Squamish legend of how the twin peaks visible from Vancouver came to be.

stories.title: Sagacious Marcela
stories.author: Filipino folktale, narrated by Lorenzo Licup; collected by Dean S. Fansler
stories.trinket: Filipino folktales paperback from a Manila bookshop
stories.contentNote: Two versions of a Filipino clever-girl tale (Pampangan + Tagalog) — both included in the file. The riddle the title comes from: the king sends Marcela one bird and demands twelve dishes from it; she sends back a single pin and demands twelve spoons made from it.
